text:
alice: Heads-up: planning a parallel backfill for feature_flags (job id: 2026-03-ff-backfill) tonight 02:00-03:30 UTC. Targeting 64 shards.
alice: I want to try parallelism to finish within window, but I’m worried about lock waves on user_profiles. Asking for ops + SRE watch and a pinned migration window via deploybot.
ben: +1 on ops watch. Can we do staggered starts per-shard instead of all 64 at once? even 8x8 waves.
carol: Staggered sounds good. Also propose we set per-job throttle: `--max-concurrency=2` and `--row-batch=1200`. That reduces lock hold time and evens out traffic.
ben: Agree. Can we also add a soft-safepoint: if more than 3 deadlocks/min or p95 latency > 350ms on writes, pause and rollback the backfill wave?
db-sre: We can add a watcher. I’ll hook up the lockwatch dashboard and alert on `deadlocks >= 3 / 1m` and write_latency_p95 > 350ms. Who should own the pause/rollback?
alice: If deploybot supports holdpoints, I’ll pin migration and request manual holdpoint on threshold. If threshold hit, ops will `deploybot pause` and we’ll resume after analysis.
carol: Command I’d use: ```
# pin and holdpoint
deploybot pin --migration=2026-03-ff-backfill --version=20260301a --holdpoint=manual
# start wave controller with stagger
backfill-controller --shards=64 --wave-size=8 --wave-delay=90s --max-concurrency=2 --row-batch=1200
```
ben: Nice. Also add a small KV prefix cache warmup on reads so we don’t spike rw path on first wave. `cache_warmup=true` in controller.
deploybot: [bot] migration 2026-03-ff-backfill pinned by alice at 1739999990. Holdpoint set to manual. To start waves run `deploybot start --migration=2026-03-ff-backfill --confirm`.
db-sre: I’ll watch the `lockwatch` Grafana panel and tail the replica lag dashboard. I’ll post RAG if anything crosses thresholds.
carol: Quick SQL check you can run during watch: ```
select shard_id, state, processed_rows, last_lock_event
from backfill_progress
where job_id='2026-03-ff-backfill'
order by shard_id;
```
ben: During the window we’ll run a canary on 8 shards first, then unpause for next 8 if stable. If we hit thresholds we rollback that wave only and keep the rest paused.
alice: Timeline: pin at 01:50 UTC, canary start 02:00, full waves 02:15-03:15, final verification 03:15-03:30. Ops to confirm once pin is done.
db-sre: Confirmed. I’ll be on-call 01:45-03:45 UTC. Will send alerts to #oncall-sre and ping here if anything major.
ben: I’ll prepare runbook snippets for pause/rollback: `deploybot pause --migration=2026-03-ff-backfill --wave=<n>` and `deploybot resume --migration=... --wave=<n>` plus links to rollback playbook.
alice: Thanks — please react when you’ve done preflight checks so I can trigger the pin. :thumbsup:
carol: Preflight done: DB stats look good, schema validated, sample canary query runs under 120ms. :white_check_mark:
ben: Runbook ready and linked in the deploy doc. :thumbsup:
db-sre: Lockwatch dashboards added, alerts in place. :eyes:
alice: OK I’m pinning now and will start the canary at 02:00. If anyone sees issues, call the abort and we’ll roll back the current wave only.
deploybot: [bot] start request received for migration 2026-03-ff-backfill. Waiting manual confirm.
carol: Manual confirm sent. Starting canary wave 1/8.
ben: Monitoring — p95 write latency 95ms, deadlocks 0. :thumbsup:
alice: Canary looks healthy, proceed with rolling waves.
carol: Wave 2/8 started.
db-sre: FYI small lock spike on shard 17, caught by watcher — paused wave 3 as expected. Investigating cause; looks like an unexpected long-running txn on product-import.
ben: Good catch. Pause is correct. Ops to coordinate with product-import team to kill/finish tx.
alice: We’ll keep other waves paused until shard 17 clears. No global rollback.
db-sre: Shard 17 cleared, resume wave 3.
carol: Resumed and reducing wave-size to 6 for next two waves for safety.
alice: Thanks team — final verification in 10m. Post any anomalies.
db-sre: Replica lag stable, no further deadlocks.
ben: Great job. Documenting postmortem steps and lessons learned in release notes.
alice: Closing thread after verification. :tada:
